title: Quantitative Cytotoxicity Assessment Using the Sulforhodamine B Assay
author: Francisco Stefânio Barreto
materials: Prepare stock solutions of the test compounds or experimental treatments at the desired initial concentration using an appropriate solvent (e.g., DMSO, sterile water, or culture medium), depending on compound solubility.
Time zero control (T0), as previously described.
Homogenize on a shaker for approximately 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare and Seed Cells
steps.instruction: Harvest and seed cells into 96-well plates at the appropriate density.

substeps.instruction: Remove culture medium and wash the cell layer with saline solution.

Add 0.05% trypsin (1x equivalent) and incubate for approximately 2 minutes in a CO₂ incubator (recommended volumes: 500 µL for T25 flasks, 1 mL for T75 flasks). Gently tap flask sides if cells do not detach completely.
Count cells using a Neubauer chamber to determine the volume needed for the desired number of plates.
For HCT116 cells, use a density of 4,000 cells/well or 0.4 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Dilute cells in complete medium to a final volume of 11 mL (for one plate).
Dispense 100 µL of cell suspension into each well.
Incubate the plate overnight in a CO₂ incubator to allow for complete cell adhesion.

steps.title: Establish Controls
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary control wells for the assay.

substeps.instruction: T0 Control: Designate a subset of wells to be fixed immediately without treatment to represent baseline cell biomass.
Negative Control: Treat cells with vehicle only (e.g., DMSO at final concentration ≤ 0.5% or equivalent solvent).
Blank Control: Prepare wells containing culture medium without cells for background subtraction.
Positive Control (Optional): Use a known cytotoxic agent (e.g., doxorubicin) at a defined effective concentration.

steps.title: Apply Treatments
steps.instruction: Expose adhered cells to the test compounds and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Perform serial dilutions in complete culture medium to obtain desired final concentrations, keeping solvent concentration constant across all treatments and controls.
For serial dilution-based assays, transfer the highest concentration into the first well of each row/column and perform stepwise dilutions, mixing thoroughly to avoid bubbles.
Expose seeded cells to 100 µL of each treatment per well.
Ensure each well contains a final volume of 200 µL (100 µL cell suspension + 100 µL treatment solution).
Incubate plates for a specified time (e.g., 72 hours) at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO₂.

steps.title: Fix Cells
steps.instruction: Fix cellular proteins using trichloroacetic acid (TCA).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 1,500 rpm for 5 minutes and remove the medium.
Add 100 µL of 10% TCA (4°C) to each well.
Incubate for at least 1 hour at 4°C.

steps.title: Wash and Stain Cells
steps.instruction: Wash fixed cells and stain with Sulforhodamine B (SRB).

substeps.instruction: Remove the acid and wash wells five times with 200 µL of deionized water (Milli-Q) per well.
Remove the deionized water.
Apply 100 µL of 0.4% SRB solution (diluted in 1% acetic acid) to all wells and incubate for 30 minutes.
Remove the SRB and wash five times with 1% acetic acid.
Allow the plate to air-dry until no visible moisture remains.

steps.title: Solubilize Dye and Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Extract the bound dye and quantify using spectrophotometry.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Tris base buffer by dissolving 1.21 g of Tris base in 1 L of Milli-Q water and autoclaving the solution.
Add 100 µL of 10 mM Tris base buffer to each well to solubilize the protein-bound dye.
Measure the optical density using a spectrophotometer at 564 nm or 570 nm.

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Process absorbance values to determine cytotoxicity and growth.

substeps.instruction: Subtract blank readings (B) from all experimental values: (T − B, CN − B, and T0 − B).
Classify responses based on T (test), CN (negative control), and T0 (time zero):
- Growth Stimulation: T ≥ CN.
- Cytostatic Effect: T0 ≤ T < CN. Calculate % Cell Growth = 100 × [(T − T0) / (CN − T0)].
- Cytocidal Effect: T < T0. Calculate % Cell Death = 100 × [(T − T0) / T0].
Export data to GraphPad Prism for nonlinear regression analysis (variable slope model) to calculate IC50 values.
Express results as mean ± SEM from at least three independent experiments in technical triplicates (p < 0.05 for significance via one-way ANOVA and post hoc comparisons).
